text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 15 in history:
1215 - King John of England sealed the Magna Carta, the Great Charter of English liberties, at Runnymede, near Windsor.
1330 - Edward the Black Prince, son and heir of King Edward III of England, born. He was given the name Black Prince by the French because of the terror of his campaign in the Hundred Years' War.
1467 - Philip the Good, duke of Burgundy, died. Founder of the Burgundian state that rivalled France in the 15th century.
1520 - Pope Leo X excommunicated Martin Luther by the bull "Exsurge Domine", condemning 41 of Luther's theses as heretical.
1567 - Mary, Queen of Scots, was captured at the battle of Carberry Hill, near Edinburgh, by Scottish nobles who objected to her marriage to the Earl of Bothwell.
1744 - British Admiral George Anson returned to England after circumnavigating the globe in an expedition that lasted nearly four years.
1775 - Congress elected George Washington General and Commander-in-Chief of the Army of the United Colonies.

1804 - The Twelfth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified, providing for the electoral college to elect the president and vice-president on separate ballots, thus preventing another instance like the election of 1800 when Thomas Jefferson and his running-mate tied, almost denying Jefferson the presidency.
1836 - Arkansas was admitted to the Union as the 25th state.
1843 - Edvard Grieg, Norwegian composer, born. He wrote incidental music for Ibsen's "Peer Gynt" which was influenced by Norwegian folk music.
1849 - James Knox Polk, 11th president of the United States (1845-49), died.
1866 - Prussia invaded Saxony, Hanover and Hesse in the European War.
1884 - Harry Langdon, U.S. film comedian of the silent era, born. Best remembered for "Tramp Tramp Tramp", "The Strong Man" and "Long Pants".
1888 - Frederick III, eighth King of Prussia and German emperor, died.
1914 - Yuri Andropov, Soviet president 1982-84, born. During his 15 months in power he clamped down hard on the arts, religion, dissent and corruption.
1919 - Englishmen John Alcock and Arthur Brown completed the first nonstop transatlantic flight.
1944 - U.S. troops invaded the Mariana Islands in the west Pacific Ocean, landing on Saipan.
1960 - South Korean government promulgated a new constitution introducing a parliamentary system of government.
1969 - Georges Pompidou was elected president of France.
1977 - Adolfo Suarez and his Democratic Centre coalition won the first democratic elections in Spain for 41 years.
1978 - Italian President Giovanni Leone was forced to resign over allegations of fiscal mismanagement and possible involvement in the Lockheed bribery scandal.
1988 - Pakistani President Zia-ul-Haq decreed that Sharia, the Islamic legal code, would be the supreme law in Pakistan.
1991 - Sikh militants took over two trains and killed 76 passengers, mostly Hindus, in an attempt to frighten voters into staying at home on election day in the north Indian state of Punjab.
1992 - Pro-Iranian kidnappers freed two German aid workers in Beirut after 1,127 days in captivity ending a decade-long hostage saga.
1993 - Azerbaijan's ex-communist elder statesman Geidar Aliyev completed a comeback in Baku when he was elected parliament chairman.
1994 - Israel and the Vatican established full diplomatic ties, sealing a historic accord on mutual recognition and reconciliation after centuries of bitterness between Roman Catholics and Jews.
